spans.text: Ministry for State Security, Berlin.
After exiting the building, Ange looks up at the blue sky that she so sorely missed.
And here I thought nowhere is as cold as the Soviet Union's administrative complex.
I envy those who complain about blinding sunshine.
What's the meaning of this?
AK-12 is still seething about their treatment.
A 48-hour interrogation experience?
Not even an extra minute?
Can I extend my session?
Even their weapons have been returned. Ange caresses her pistol and fights the sudden urge to charge back inside and shoot everyone.
But isn't it good that we're released?
Of course it's good, but I can't help but wonder—why?
Ange looks up at the long flight of stairs before her thoughtfully.
RPK-16 and AK-15, who were the first to leave the building, are now sitting at the bottom of the staircase.
RPK-16 is tapping away at the laptop computer she is balancing on her knees. A cable joins the two Dolls by the neck.
Were you all locked up in separate cells?
Ange shuffles down the stairs slowly and sits down next to her subordinates.
Neural cloud...okay.
Fire-control core...okay.
Sorry, what was that again?
Yes, I was held inside an electronically-sealed room.
But they didn't do anything to me.
Apparently, they were worried that the four of us would be violent in our resistance.
Which is ridiculous—if we had wanted to raise hell, it would make no difference whether we were locked together or separately.
How long was I in there? Two days?
It's been more than two days since we got off the plane.
While we were held captive, they wouldn't let us see anyone, nor were we allowed visitors.
All our equipment and weapons were also confiscated.
I honestly thought we would only walk out of there to have our neural clouds fried.
What do you make of this, Ange?
The detention was uncharacteristically short. It should've lasted at least another week.
They obviously have no qualms about torture, but they ended up releasing me before they could beat the information out of me. That's very odd.
True, we shouldn't count on the Germans suddenly developing a conscience.
Someone pulled some strings behind the scenes.
Our release definitely wasn't a coincidence.
Could it be Chairwoman Ulrich?
If Ulrich had that much power, we wouldn't have ended up in this sticky situation in the very first place.
...48 hours is more than enough for Morridow to make it across the border into the Soviet Union.
I heard that Mr. K has taken over the investigation.
AK-15 suddenly opens her eyes and joins the conversation. RPK-16 deftly unplugs the cable from her neck.
Take a seat, Captain.
No thanks, I can run a diagnostic on my own.
We've been held for two whole days. If they messed around with our hardware or software, you'd want to find out now, so stop being a sulky child.
You do realize that as things stand, there's no way we can find even cheap replacements for our bodies, right?
AK-12 sits down grumpily at the spot previously occupied by AK-15.
K took over... I have nothing against him.
But they might as well have lined the streets and given Morridow a warm send-off across the border.
We wouldn't catch her in time even if we set off now.
I know. Not to mention that these Krauts are restricting my movements.
Ange rests her hands on her knees and slowly scans the empty streets around her.
Who knows how many hidden pairs of eyes are currently observing the group having a conversation on the stairs.
They had to keep a low profile even though they're on their home turf...
Looks like whoever helped us is of considerable status and authority.
All this speculation does us no good. Even without all these obstacles, we still need time to rest.
Willpower is all that's keeping Miss Ange on her feet in her present condition.
You're in no state to continue our investigation, are you?
RPK-16 leans towards Ange affectionately and takes a long, deliberate look at her quivering legs.
AK-12 forcefully yanks the cable connecting her to RPK-16 and jerks her back.
I'm with her on this one, Ange.
You can play tough all you want in front of others, but you sound like you want to get back to work in your current state.
Not only is that reckless, it's downright stupid.
...We've already wasted too much time.
Ange glares at her knees and growls defiantly.
Then what difference does a few more hours make?
You said it yourself—you thought they were going to keep you for at least a week.
But it's only been 48 hours—plus a few more hours of sleep.
We're actually ahead of schedule.
...Fine.
But before I rest...
Nobody objects to some light workout, hm?
Ange gives her thighs a smack and slowly stands up.
RPK-16 unplugs the cable and gestures to AK-12 that the diagnostic is complete. She jokes jovially as she packs away her equipment.
My, so Ange likes toying with young men.
She looks around thoughtfully and makes a face in the direction that Ange was squinting at.
Don't put it so weirdly.
...Two on the left, three on the right.
About eight in the building behind us.
What should we do with them?
Let's give them a lesson and teach them to show some respect to veterans.
Give these Krauts hell.
Yes, ma'am.
